context: The prompt requests making the work iteration registry directly visible in the Workdir section of the Web UI with view-only access. The registry is currently stored in JSON format at `.rdd-instance/workdir/work-iteration-registry.json` and contains information about the iteration, prompts, and their states. The goal is to improve user visibility by parsing and presenting this data in a human-readable format within the existing Workdir page.

questions.question-text: How should the registry be displayed in the Workdir section?

options.label: Replace the current compact status header with a comprehensive registry view that shows all prompts in a table format
options.pros: Maximum information density, shows all prompts at once, eliminates redundancy with the compact status
options.cons: Removes the compact summary which may be useful for quick reference, could be overwhelming for iterations with many prompts

options.label: Add a new expandable card below the current status header that shows the full registry when expanded
options.pros: Preserves the existing compact status, users can expand/collapse as needed, clean default view
options.cons: Requires an extra click to see details, adds vertical scrolling when expanded

options.label: Replace the File Viewer section with a dedicated Registry Viewer that shows the registry in formatted view
options.pros: Dedicated space for registry, removes redundant file viewer that can still be accessed via button, cleaner interface
options.cons: Removes generic file viewing capability from the Workdir page, users would need to use other methods to view files

options.label: Add a new tab-based view in the Workdir section with tabs for Status, Registry, and File Viewer
options.pros: Organized separation of concerns, preserves all functionality, allows each section to use full width
options.cons: More complex UI, requires additional navigation (clicking tabs), may feel heavier

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option B provides the best balance by preserving the existing compact status for quick reference while adding detailed registry information on demand. It's a non-destructive change that enhances functionality without removing existing features, and users can choose their preferred level of detail.

questions.question-text: What information should be displayed for each prompt in the registry view?

options.label: Minimal: prompt-id, title, state only
options.pros: Clean and simple, reduces visual clutter, focuses on essentials, easy to scan
options.cons: Missing important metadata like execution mode and completion flags, limited usefulness

options.label: Standard: prompt-id, title, state, execution-mode, and all boolean flags (questionnaire-generated, questionnaire-answered, plan-generated, analysis-generated, implementation-completed, executed)
options.pros: Comprehensive overview of each prompt's progress, shows workflow status, helps users track what's been done
options.cons: More columns make table wider, may require horizontal scrolling on smaller screens

options.label: Extended: All standard fields plus current-modification-id (when applicable)
options.pros: Complete picture including modifications, most informative view, shows everything in registry
options.cons: Very wide table, information overload for simple use cases, modification ID only relevant for some prompts

options.label: Adaptive: Minimal by default with an expand button per row to show additional details
options.pros: Combines cleanliness with flexibility, users see more detail only when needed, responsive-friendly
options.cons: More complex to implement, requires additional interaction, details are hidden by default

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option B provides essential workflow information that users need to understand prompt progress without being overwhelming. The boolean flags are critical for understanding which execution steps have been completed. While modification-id is useful, it's only relevant for a subset of prompts, so including it in every row (Option C) adds unnecessary width.

questions.question-text: How should boolean flags (questionnaire-generated, executed, etc.) be displayed?

options.label: Text: 'true' / 'false' in each column
options.pros: Explicit and unambiguous, no learning curve, accessible for screen readers
options.cons: Verbose and takes up space, less visually appealing, harder to scan quickly

options.label: Icons: Checkmark for true, X or empty for false
options.pros: Compact and space-efficient, visually scannable, modern look, color-coded (green checkmark, red X)
options.cons: Requires icon legend or tooltips, may be less accessible without proper ARIA labels

options.label: Badges: Green 'Yes' badge for true, gray 'No' badge for false
options.pros: Clear visual distinction, self-explanatory, accessible, combines text and color
options.cons: Takes more space than icons, may feel redundant, less compact

options.label: Colored dots: Green dot for true, gray dot for false (similar to Active Prompt page flags)
options.pros: Very compact, consistent with existing UI patterns in the application, clean minimal look
options.cons: Less self-documenting, requires tooltips to explain meaning, not ideal without context

questions.recommendation-rationale: Icons with tooltips provide the best balance between space efficiency and clarity. Using checkmark/X icons with color coding (green/red or green/gray) is an industry-standard pattern that users recognize immediately. Adding ARIA labels and tooltips ensures accessibility while keeping the interface clean and scannable.

questions.question-text: Should the iteration metadata (iteration-id, iteration-name, prompt-id-sequence-next-value, git-enabled) be displayed separately from the prompts list?

options.label: Yes, show iteration metadata in a separate section at the top of the registry view
options.pros: Clear separation between iteration-level and prompt-level data, easier to find iteration info, logical organization
options.cons: Adds vertical space, may duplicate the existing compact status header

options.label: No, integrate iteration metadata into the compact status header and focus the registry view on prompts only
options.pros: Avoids duplication, keeps registry view focused on prompts, cleaner layout
options.cons: Iteration metadata might not be visible when compact status is replaced, less comprehensive

options.label: Display iteration metadata in the registry card header as part of the title
options.pros: Always visible, consolidated presentation, uses existing card header space efficiently
options.cons: Header might become crowded, less flexibility in formatting metadata

questions.recommendation-rationale: If using an expandable card approach (from Q1-B), showing iteration metadata separately at the top of the expanded view provides clear context before diving into the prompts list. This creates a logical hierarchy: iteration info first, then individual prompts. The slight duplication with the compact status is acceptable since the compact view remains for quick glances while the detailed view serves comprehensive inspection.

questions.question-text: Should the registry view provide any interactive features or remain strictly read-only?

options.label: Strictly read-only: Display data only with no interactive elements
options.pros: Aligns with 'view only' requirement, simplest implementation, no risk of accidental changes
options.cons: Limited functionality, users can't quickly jump to prompts or perform actions

options.label: Read-only with navigation: Add clickable prompt titles that navigate to the prompt in Prompts History page
options.pros: Enhances usability, provides quick navigation, data remains protected from editing, common UX pattern
options.cons: Slightly more complex than pure read-only, requires coordination between pages

options.label: Read-only with actions: Include view/edit buttons for each prompt similar to Prompts History page
options.pros: Maximally useful, consolidates functionality, users can act on prompts directly from Workdir
options.cons: May blur the purpose of different pages, duplicates functionality of Prompts History

questions.recommendation-rationale: Making prompt titles clickable to navigate to the Prompts History page strikes a good balance between maintaining the view-only nature of the registry display while adding useful navigation. This is a common UX pattern that users expect, and it doesn't compromise the read-only requirement since the registry itself isn't editable - it just provides links to existing functionality.
